description:
FILED AND FIXED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20), found by a CHECK-2 probe on
t/op/magic.t's description-building block (magic.t:591).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL before the fix):

    foreach (['powie::!', 'Errno']) {
        my ($symbol, $package) = @$_;
        print "symbol=[$symbol] package=[$package] n=", scalar(@$_), "\n";
    }

    perl: symbol=[powie::!] package=[Errno] n=2        (ONE iteration)
    PCL:  symbol=[] package=[] n=0                      (TWICE)
          symbol=[] package=[] n=0

The loop ran ONCE PER ELEMENT of the referent, with `$_` bound to the element
("powie::!" then "Errno"), so `@$_` was a SYMBOLIC array deref of that string
-- empty -- and every use of the unpacked variables was silently wrong.  A
HASH constructor did the same (`for ({a=>1}) { %$_ }` iterated the key and
then the value).

MECHANISM: #267's rule -- a foreach list whose every depth-0 element is a
single SCALAR operand emits `(vector ...)` instead of going through
`%p-flatten-for-list`, because at RUNTIME a box wrapping a vector is
indistinguishable from an @array box.  `Pl::Parser::_foreach_single_scalar_p`
accepted a `$`-Symbol, a `${...}` block and a `\`-cast term, but NOT a
`PPI::Structure::Constructor`.  An anonymous constructor is exactly as
unambiguously ONE value as `$x` is, and the sigil is compile-time knowledge,
so it belongs in the same predicate -- ONE arm, no new mechanism.

FIX: one `elsif` in `_foreach_single_scalar_p` (a Constructor primary
qualifies unless a `$` cast precedes it -- `${[...]}` is a deref).

MEASURED
  * 18 probe shapes vs perl (`probes/p7.pl`): 16 identical; 6 of them
    (`for ({...})`, `for ([])`, `for ({})`, the nested constructor, the
    statement-modifier spelling and the `my @c = @$_` shape) FAIL on a
    `268d7e00` extraction.
  * The k>1 spelling `for ([1],[2,3])` already ANSWERED right (p-flatten-args
    keeps a box as one element) but went through the flattener; it now takes
    the direct `(vector ...)` path, which is what the corpus diff shows.
  * corpus emission: 4 files of 111 -- `perl-tests/bop.t`, `magic.t`,
    `method.t`, `split.t` -- every diff the same shape
    (`(p-flatten-args (list <ctor boxes>))` / `(make-p-box (p-array-init ...))`
    -> `(vector <ctor boxes>)`); lib A/B 27 SAME / 0 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF.
  * Guard `Pl/t/foreach-aliasing-01.t` 22 -> 30 rows, 5 of the 8 failing on
    the base, 2 of the others being inverse guards (`@{[...]}` and
    `keys %{{...}}` must KEEP flattening) and 1 a net.

NEIGHBOURS FOUND BY THE SAME PROBE, both PRE-EXISTING (identical on the base)
and NOT fixed here -- they are the same runtime ambiguity in a consumer the
emitter cannot reach:
  * `for (mk()) { ref $_ }` where `sub mk { return [1,2] }` -- a sub RETURNING
    a reference is flattened by the foreach list.  perl `ARRAY`, PCL empty.
    No sigil to read: the value is only known at runtime.  -> #1955.
  * `map { ref } [1,2]` answers the empty string twice; that is #1991's
    family (a backslashed array in a map/grep/sort argument list), filed by
    the s492a batch.

=== DONE (s473t6d) ===
Shipped with the bars above.

COMPANION LEG (member 4, finished s493): the same two invented rows are visible
in the companion population -- t/op/magic.t 176/31 -> 174/31 and its shortfall
1 -> 3 (the never-produced SET is unchanged; the metric is perl's row count
minus PCL's, and the two surplus rows had been padding PCL's).  The numbering
offset the fix removes takes the renumber marker from 82 rows to 7, which
re-aligned ONE blessed diverging row onto the perl row it really is: the
failure is `eval " BEGIN { ok ! defined $^S } "` at magic.t:615, not
`${^TAINT}` at :619 -- filed as #1968.
subject: SILENT WRONG (everyday): `for ([1,2]) {...}` iterates the REFERENT -- an anonymous ARRAY/HASH constructor in a foreach list was flattened, so the loop ran once per ELEMENT with $_ bound to the element
